prose.text: The chunk's own guard and pins come first, then the two live entries, then the standard gate set in test-plan §3 order (`capability-drift` before the default-features workspace nextest, the `--features mcp-server` bindings regen as the last cargo-adjacent step, the base-identity bindings close, since the chunk adds no procedure), then the local pre-push check with its teardown probe, then the operator pass.

**The window smoke** is listed because the window program's `boot` reads readiness through the changed decision. It is the series of two boots on this host in its recorded form: each under its own virtual display, the receivers on 14317 and 14318, `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` unset, a fresh data dir under `target/boot-smoke/`.
**The engine cycle** is the console engine's runtime gate, on ports 24317 and 24318 and a fresh data dir under `target/engine-cycle/`. Its kept log is the real log step 8's mutations are read on.

**The pre-push check** now runs a cycle of its own on the same two ports, so it never runs beside the engine cycle entry: the gate tool fires entries one at a time. The probe after it reads that the stage ended what it started.

**One-shot mutating control** (check 4 (6)): step 8's seven mutations are run once at implement, both readings of each in `evidence/mutations.md`. On every re-run the property is guarded by two listed entries that mutate nothing: the scope guard, which reads red on any change left in `xtask/src/engine_log.rs`, and the workspace nextest, which runs the module's pins.

Absences, each with its reason: - No product boot-path file is touched (`main.rs`, `engine_boot.rs`, `console.rs`, `observability.rs`), so no   boot-smoke gate is owed for the product; the two live entries are the harness's own. - No webview gate and no headful self-verify: no `pulse-app/ui/**` path is touched. - No local `cargo audit` or `cargo deny` entry: no dependency is added and the scope guard holds `Cargo.lock`   unchanged; the `supply-chain` job reads both on the operator pass's run. - No live reading of a taken port on 24317 or 24318 in this block: the refusal is pinned on the built verb with   the test's own listener on a picked port, so no gate entry holds a registered harness port. - No retry anywhere. A cycle that reads red, a boot that ended by itself or a port found taken stops the pass   and goes to the operator.

**The operator pass, in this order.** The hygiene entry; the pre-CI commit; the local pre-push check again; the merge-base probe; the build-branch push; the CI read of the pushed tip, asserted green; the run's `logs-boot-Linux` artifact (the window program's eight boots under the changed readiness); the run's `logs-engine-Linux` artifact, graded again by `check:engine-log` on this host. A line of a witness file holding anything beyond its shape stops the pass. A red is fixed by a further commit on top and read again.
